meta.title: Vornik — build agent swarms that you own
meta.description: Vornik runs AI agent teams on your own machine. Use it for autonomous work that runs while you're away, or to give your coding agent memory, skills and a team. Install it by handing one prompt to your coding agent.
meta.socialDescription: Autonomous AI work and assisted coding on one self-hosted daemon. Install it by handing one prompt to your coding agent.

theme.title: Switch light / dark
hero.eyebrow: Adds memory, skills and workflows to your agents
hero.title: Build agent swarms that you own.
hero.lede: One self-hosted daemon. Your agents, your servers, your rules.
install.prompt: Set up Vornik for me. Follow the runbook at https://agents.vornik.io
install.agentNote: Paste it into Claude Code, Codex, or your Hermes agent with shell access.
install.reassure: Free and open source. Linux and macOS. No account, no cloud sign-up.
ways.title: One install, two ways to work
ways.lede: Most people start with one and end up using both, on the same daemon and memory.
ways.label: Use case
ways.autonomous: Autonomous AI<small>work that runs without you</small>
auto.description: Teams of agents start from a goal, schedule, webhook or GitHub event, and pause only where you ask for approval.
auto.review: Review every pull request, fix labelled issues
auto.inbox: Watch an inbox, draft calendar events
auto.connects: Talk to it from Telegram, email or the web UI.
auto.line1: forge       task queued for the dev team
auto.line2: researcher  reads the code and project memory
auto.line3: developer   writes the fix, tests pass
auto.line4: reviewer    checks the diff and CI
auto.line7: needs you send the refund request? approved on phone
auto.accessible: Example: a labelled GitHub issue starts a task; researcher, developer and reviewer agents fix it and open a pull request. A weekday schedule runs an inbox digest, asks for approval on the phone before sending an email, and delivers the summary to Telegram.
code.description: Your coding agent gets persistent project memory, shared skills, and a team to hand reviews and research to while it keeps working.
code.recall: Recall why code is built the way it is
code.review: Get a review after each commit
code.skills: Turn a one-off fix into a skill for every session
code.connects: Plugin for Claude Code and Codex; any CLI works over HTTP.
code.line2: 3 notes found, incl. why leases expire
code.line5: queued on Vornik, keeps coding meanwhile
code.line6: ok  review came back green, 0 findings
code.line7: remember "root cause: clock skew on renewal"
code.line8: ok  stored for the next session
code.accessible: Example: in Claude Code, the agent recalls prior design notes from Vornik memory, makes a fix, delegates an architectural review to Vornik while it keeps working, gets a green review back, and stores the root cause for the next session.
steps.title: Your coding agent does the install
steps.lede: The runbook at agents.vornik.io is written for agents. You approve anything privileged.
steps.oneText: Into Claude Code, Codex or your Hermes agent.
steps.twoText: Daemon, database, your model key, and a first task that must complete.
steps.threeText: Your agent gets its own project and memory for next time.
setup.accessible: A coding agent installing Vornik: it runs the installer, verifies readiness, submits a first task that completes, and confirms its memory round-trip.
setup.heading: your agent · setting up vornik
setup.line0: > Set up Vornik for me. Follow agents.vornik.io
setup.line2: ok  Vornik is up and ready.
setup.line6: ok  task COMPLETED, the agent answered
core.title: The same core under both
core.lede: One host you control, and every result is kept.
core.hostText: A home server, mini-PC or rented box. Linux or macOS.
core.modelText: Open-weight or OpenAI-compatible, picked per role.
core.isolationText: Every agent in its own container, optionally with no network.
core.memoryText: Searchable per-project memory that builds on earlier work.
core.approvalText: Approval gates, answered on your paired phone.
core.restartText: A crash or reboot puts the work back in the queue.
editions.title: Free to run, open to read
editions.lede: Community is the complete core, not a demo.
editions.communityText: Daemon, agents, memory, workflows, web UI, CLI and plugins.
editions.enterpriseText: Clustering, SSO, admin suite and commercial support on the same core.
final.title: Install Vornik in one prompt
final.lede: A working daemon, a finished first task and an agent that remembers, in minutes.
footer.tagline: Agent swarms that you own. Open core, AGPL-3.0.
install.shellNote: Linux with rootless Podman, or macOS (the script sets up a small Linux VM with Lima). It installs the daemon, PostgreSQL with pgvector and a user service; a first-run guide at localhost:8080/ui/setup then connects your model. Verify the script first.
